primitives.name: Total Pace Component
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Pace is defined from the distance traveled by the puck between successive possession events by the same team, divided by elapsed time, decomposed into components: **φT** (total speed), **φEW** (east-west), **φNS** (north-south), **φN** (north-only; backward movement counted as zero).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'φT': 'total pace component (ft/s)', 'Δd': 'change in puck distance (ft)', 'Δt': 'elapsed time (s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Puck trajectory approximates team movement; temporal resolution captures meaningful possession events.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When possession events are infrequent or non-consecutive, φT becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: φT serves as base metric for spatial and temporal variance in team behavior, used in GSE's state transition matrices for simulated puck movement.
layer2.telemetry: Average pace per game across zones, validated via cross-correlation with shot quality.

primitives.name: Zone Differential Pace
primitives.verbatim_quote: Analysis is zonal (offensive/defensive/neutral zone) and spatial via a **polygrid**: the rink divided into **668 cells of 5×5 feet**, with 2D Gaussian smoothing (**σ = 0.5**) producing team-vs-league-average differential pace maps.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Δφzone': 'pace differential by zone (ft/s)', 'φteam,zone': 'team-specific zone pace (ft/s)', 'φleague,zone': 'league average zone pace (ft/s)'}
primitives.assumptions: League averages are stable over time; spatial smoothing preserves local structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In low-volume games or rare events, differential maps may be noisy or unrepresentative.

layer2.mapping: Zone differentials mirror NFL field position effects on scoring probability, enabling GSE to map rink zones to yard-line equivalents.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between zone pace and expected goal rate per zone.

primitives.name: Player-Level Pace (WOWY)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Player-level pace with WOWY (with-or-without-you) on/off splits (minimum 200 minutes 5v5).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'φplayer^WOWY': 'player pace under WOWY framework (ft/s)', 'di': 'distance traveled during possession i (ft)', 'ti': 'time duration of possession i (s)'}
primitives.assumptions: WOWY isolates individual contribution; 5v5 context ensures comparable baseline.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Insufficient playing time (<200 min) invalidates WOWY estimates.

layer2.mapping: Player pace under WOWY enables GSE to simulate lineup impacts on tempo and outcome likelihood.
layer2.telemetry: Change in pace when player enters/exits 5v5 situations.

This is decomposed into directional components φEW, φNS, and φN to capture anisotropic motion. These metrics are aggregated across rink zones using a polygrid approach with 2D Gaussian smoothing to produce spatially resolved pace maps. The WOWY method isolates player-level contributions by comparing performance with and without specific players. However, these operators lack predictive power due to absence of supervised learning, out-of-sample validation, or calibration against market outcomes. The failure mode lies in assuming that hockey-specific pace correlates with NFL game dynamics, which lacks empirical grounding. The paper’s descriptive focus precludes GSE’s requirement for causal inference and forecasting accuracy.
